authoredFrom: BD-ref-target: a `$ref` names a LOCATION, not a symbol, so the target is `Refs.definitions.Node` and not the bare `Node`. Nothing guarantees the name at a location is unique - two documents in one file can each declare `spec` - while the location itself is. The SOURCE is the `$ref` occurrence's own path for the same reason, which is why one endpoint in this file resolves by qualifiedName rather than by name; that is recorded in the lane's gap note rather than papered over here. `contains` endpoints are QUALIFIED PATHS: this pin set was migrated from bare-name endpoints by a structure-preserving transformation (owner and child and line unchanged, spelling resolved against the fixture's own qualifiedName). The reason is measured, not stylistic: over a 202-file, 99-repo sample 32,660 of 66,032 `contains` edges (49.4%) named a target matching MORE THAN ONE published symbol, and the shared resolver declines a non-unique bare name, so those edges bound to no declaration at all. See meta.endpoints=qualified_path on the edge.
